arguments: Operation slot can be leaked on cipher finish failure
message.text: Operation slot can be leaked on cipher finish failure

properties.metisTriageReason: Verdict: cipher finish failure leaves the TF-M multipart operation slot allocated instead of taking the release path. Evidence: finish success jumps to release at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:300 and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:302, while failure only clears output length at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:303 and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:304 before returning at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:317; the release label calls tfm_crypto_operation_release at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:319 and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_cipher.c:321, and release is what marks a finite operation slot not in use at secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:50, secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:141, and secure_fw/partitions/crypto/crypto_alloc.c:142. Gap: none.
properties.mitigation: On finish failure states that invalidate or abort the underlying PSA operation, release the TF-M operation slot just as the update-error path does. If some finish errors are recoverable by contract, distinguish recoverable output-buffer-too-small cases from terminal failures and document/handle the lifetime accordingly, possibly requiring explicit abort for recoverable cases with quota protections.
properties.reasoning: On successful finish, the TF-M multipart operation slot is released, and on update failure the code comments that the PSA operation aborts and explicitly releases the slot. In contrast, if psa_cipher_finish returns an error, this path only clears out_vec[1].len and then returns status without releasing the TF-M operation slot. Depending on PSA semantics for cipher_finish failures and whether callers can repeatedly create operations that fail at finish (for example through insufficient output buffers or invalid padding), a client may exhaust the finite multipart operation table in the secure crypto partition, causing denial of service to itself or other clients sharing the pool. The precise cross-client impact depends on operation-table ownership and quota enforcement outside this file.
